destination.title: De Sitter backgrounds: existence, stability and control
destination.question: Under which source-specific ingredients and approximations can compactifications or related constructions support de Sitter geometry, and what establishes their stability, consistency and effective control?
destination.summary: The original parent has numerical membership but no written scientific scope to endorse. Its contrasts support separate questions about existence, asymptotic control, source matching, evolving quantum backgrounds, effective potentials and statistical stability. Overlapping child-batch titles should not become redundant public branches. Existing scoped questions provide shared destinations across those batches, with distinct applications and alternate homes retained.

systems: Type II compactifications and their related M-theory descriptions
Other string constructions represented in the attributed child reviews
Sourced higher-dimensional gravity and effective supergravity models, with embedding qualifications retained
targets: De Sitter geometry, positive stationary potentials and candidate minima
Moduli stabilization and perturbative or dynamical stability
Source consistency, correction control and finite versus parametric limits
Effective potentials, quantum expansions and state interpretations
Source-defined vacuum statistics and conditional cosmological applications
regimes: Classical, perturbatively corrected and nonperturbative settings kept distinct
Static and evolving internal configurations
Finite parameter values and asymptotic families
Source-specific external dimensions and retained field sectors
AdS and Minkowski comparisons where explicitly supplied
assumptions: Each construction and obstruction retains its own source content, ansatz and approximation
Necessary conditions do not establish solutions, stability or control
Numerical ancestry does not determine scientific parentage
Descendant coverage is attributed to child ledgers rather than independently established by this parent pass
conventions: Positive curvature, a stationary potential, a positive-definite retained Hessian and a controlled metastable vacuum are different claims
Frames, scalar normalization, source signs and coupling definitions remain source-specific
Graph relations describe exact source objects and do not automatically impose premises on a question
Source-scoped singleton access establishes neither atomicity nor cross-source uniqueness
includes: Ordinary and pre-Swampland construction and stability research
Conditional, unsuccessful and disputed proposals with their status preserved
Shared target routes across numerical child batches
Methods, comparisons and applications with explicit relationship types

A present-day census inferred from dated source statements

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: How do intersecting source sets change the existence restrictions derived for parallel sources?

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Are omitted bulk and localized terms suppressed in hierarchical LVS, and can BPS charge–tension matching forbid candidate induced potentials?

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: Can calculations or symmetries exclude mixed-cycle and higher-loop terms that are less suppressed than the retained α′ effect?

sources.title: More about F-term uplifting

evidence.text: Can an independently stabilized, heavier modulus prevent the large relative X displacement induced by a modulus-dependent uplifting tadpole?

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: When can string-loop corrections be neglected in moduli stabilization? The survey distinguishes corrections that bound a mechanism's validity from corrections that generate its stabilizing potential, and it warns that conclusions drawn from a few-modulus model need not survive additional flat directions.

sources.title: Universal de Sitter solutions at tree-level

evidence.text: Can classical four-dimensional de Sitter solutions of type IIA compactification be constructed directly in ten dimensions using only universal SU(3)-structure forms and torsion classes, and can an explicit geometry satisfy the resulting conditions?

sources.title: Supersymmetry breaking branes on solvmanifolds and de Sitter vacua in string theory

evidence.text: Can classical geometric type IIA compactifications with sources breaking bulk supersymmetry yield ten-dimensional de Sitter solutions, and can generalized first-order equations simplify their construction?

sources.title: A note on obstinate tachyons in classical dS solutions

evidence.text: Do the persistent tachyons in classical geometric de Sitter compactifications have a structural explanation in volume, dilaton and orientifold-cycle fluctuations, and how does this explanation connect to the sgoldstino near a supersymmetric limit?

sources.title: Extended No-Scale Structure and $\alpha^{'2}$ Corrections to the Type IIB Action

evidence.text: How does the previously derived GSW string-tree-level α′² correction affect perturbative control and survival of KKLT, LVS and Kähler-uplifted vacua, despite extended no-scale cancellation?

sources.title: Compactifying de Sitter space naturally selects a small cosmological constant

evidence.text: Does compactifying a positive-cosmological-constant higher-dimensional theory on multiple dynamical flux-supported spheres produce a distribution of lower-dimensional de Sitter vacua that accumulates at zero cosmological constant?

sources.title: de Sitter Vacua in Type IIB String Theory: Classical Solutions and Quantum Corrections

evidence.text: Can ten-dimensional type IIB compactifications with fluxes and localized sources yield four-dimensional de Sitter geometry, and what conditions must quantum curvature corrections satisfy to evade classical obstructions?

sources.title: Constraining de Sitter Space in String Theory

evidence.text: Can classical heterotic string theory realize maximally symmetric de Sitter vacua once all world-sheet effects, including high-curvature physics, are included? Which assumptions or omitted quantum effects could evade a world-sheet obstruction?

sources.title: Refining the boundaries of the classical de Sitter landscape

evidence.text: Which classical de Sitter solutions can exist in ten-dimensional type II supergravity with spacetime-filling Dp/Op sources of one fixed dimension, principally with parallel sources? The target is existence, without a four-dimensional stability analysis.

sources.title: On classical de Sitter and Minkowski solutions with intersecting branes

evidence.text: Which classical type II compactifications with intersecting Dp-branes and Op-planes permit four-dimensional de Sitter or Minkowski solutions, and how does source overlap constrain their existence?

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Can positive critical points in string compactifications test the conjecture within a regime whose corrections and flux quantization are controlled?

sources.title: New constraints on classical de Sitter: flirting with the swampland

evidence.text: Does the unsuccessful search reflect an actual obstruction to de Sitter solutions, and which equations would establish that obstruction?

sources.title: The quantum swampland

evidence.text: Can controlled string constructions support metastable positive vacuum energy? The reviewed obstacles concern classical type II solutions, flux quantization, nonperturbative stabilization, and antibrane uplifts, with explicit disagreement in the cited literature.

sources.title: Weakly Coupled de Sitter Vacua with Fluxes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can classical type IIA fluxes and localized sources stabilize the universal volume and inverse string coupling in a parametrically controlled de Sitter regime? The displayed potential supplies the common setting for the explicit no-go arguments.

sources.title: Scaling limits of dS vacua and the swampland

evidence.text: Do suitable orientifold geometries admit large O6-plane counts, and do any realize de Sitter extrema at large volume and weak coupling? The formal source-count scaling motivates this question without resolving geometric existence or the size of a possible upper bound.

sources.title: Classical de Sitter Solutions of 10-Dimensional Supergravity

evidence.text: Can massive type IIA supergravity admit four-dimensional de Sitter compactifications obtained directly from the full ten-dimensional equations with localized, backreacted orientifolds, and how far can weak coupling and small curvature justify their classical description?

sources.title: Modular symmetries and the swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Does adding a dilaton-like chiral field change the extrema found in the single-modulus model?

sources.title: On Stringy de Sitter Spacetimes

evidence.text: What do axilaton deformations imply about 3+1-dimensional de Sitter backgrounds in string theory, their supersymmetric limits and duality patching, and the need for string degrees of freedom beyond a tree-level spacetime effective description?

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Does the selected scalar sector reveal a tachyon in every classical de Sitter solution with intersecting sources?

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Can a classical de Sitter supergravity solution satisfy weak coupling, large physical lengths, flux quantization, and bounded orientifold availability simultaneously?

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Can classical type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources support four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime? The paper fixes a commonly used smeared compactification ansatz to formulate existence, stability, and string-control questions.

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Must every classical de Sitter solution with intersecting Op/Dp sources contain a scalar direction of negative mass squared?

sources.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

evidence.text: Does the restricted classical type II compactification problem admit a de Sitter solution when every Op/Dp source is parallel?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: Which restrictions on classical compactifications make de Sitter exclusion possible? The setting separates the two-derivative positive-tension regime from constructions containing orientifolds, curvature, or string-scale corrections.

sources.title: Logarithmic loop corrections, moduli stabilisation and de Sitter vacua in string theory

evidence.text: Why is stabilization of an expansion modulus difficult in a perturbative regime? The reviewed argument attributes the problem to monotonic finite-order potentials whose competing terms become comparable only when the expansion parameter ceases to be small.

sources.title: dS Spaces and Brane Worlds in Exotic String Theories

evidence.text: Can a Lorentzian-string orientifold retain wrong-sign closed fields that evade a de Sitter no-go argument while supporting an ordinary four-dimensional gauge coefficient?

sources.title: Jumping Through Loops: On Soft Terms from Large Volume Compactifications

evidence.text: The proposed diagnostic compares a candidate DBI-induced tension with a corresponding Chern–Simons charge term under BPS assumptions. Applying it to the listed flux–curvature terms remains heuristic.

sources.title: More about F-term uplifting

evidence.text: Integrate out heavy modes near the supersymmetry-breaking configuration and retain the leading quartic Kähler correction together with a linear effective superpotential.

sources.title: Systematics of String Loop Corrections in Type IIB Calabi-Yau Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: Estimate the surviving Coleman–Weinberg powers using a gravitino mass and a sector cutoff, then compare them with the corrected Kähler potential. The procedure tests parametric consistency and must be accompanied by an effective-theory hierarchy check.

sources.title: Universal de Sitter solutions at tree-level

evidence.text: For group manifolds, use left-invariant Maurer–Cartan forms, orientifold parity, Jacobi identities and a previously derived de Sitter no-go criterion to restrict candidate algebras. The authors then test torsion constraints on four candidate algebras.

sources.title: Supersymmetry breaking branes on solvmanifolds and de Sitter vacua in string theory

evidence.text: Reduce to a four-dimensional Einstein-frame potential for volume ρ and dilaton σ=ρ^(3/2)e^(−φ̃). Different volume scalings of X components generate additional source terms b1 and b2.

sources.title: A note on obstinate tachyons in classical dS solutions

evidence.text: The authors examine Hessian minors restricted to selected scalar directions. A negative eigenvalue of such a restriction establishes an instability of the full critical point; increasingly large restrictions identify a small subspace sufficient to detect the observed instabilities.

sources.title: Weakly Coupled de Sitter Vacua with Fluxes and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can flux compactifications support de Sitter minima while a control parameter improves without bound? The paper separates this asymptotic question from the existence of individual vacua at finite large volume and weak coupling.

sources.title: No classical (anti-)de Sitter solutions with O8-planes

evidence.text: Can classical Type IIA compactifications with only O8-planes/D8-branes support de Sitter space, and can singular source behavior justify the boundary conditions used in proposed numerical de Sitter and Romans-mass-only anti-de Sitter solutions?

sources.title: de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Can time-dependent compactification geometry, fluxes and quantum corrections support four-dimensional de Sitter isometries with constant Newton coupling and a controlled effective field theory, despite obstructions found for time-independent internal configurations?

sources.title: The web of swampland conjectures and the TCC bound

evidence.text: Which classical ingredients obstruct a positive stationary four-dimensional potential in type II compactifications? The analysis separates universal moduli, source-aligned anisotropies, and a single internal radius.

sources.title: UV Shadows in EFTs: Accidental Symmetries, Robustness and No‐Scale Supergravity

evidence.text: Why do perturbative string compactifications so often yield no-scale supergravity, and which quantum or α′ corrections first lift its flat potentials? The authors seek symmetry-based constraints that assess the robustness of moduli stabilization and explain classical de Sitter obstructions.

sources.title: A Global View on The Search for de-Sitter Vacua in (type IIA) String Theory

evidence.text: How unlikely is a tachyon-free de Sitter extremum in classical Type IIA searches, and does raising vacuum energy destabilize initially positive-mass configurations through increased moduli mixing?

evidence.text: Can freezing and restoration of charged-state Krylov spreading provide a quantum-information diagnostic of extremal black-hole discharge associated with the Weak Gravity Conjecture (WGC)?

sources.title: Freezing Swampland: A Krylov Complexity Criterion for the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Evaluate the scalar Gaussian determinant with a proper-time heat kernel. A locally constant electric field produces proper-time poles whose residues yield an imaginary effective action and vacuum decay; Appendix C compares this estimate with a reviewed global AdS2 spectral treatment.

sources.title: Freezing Swampland: A Krylov Complexity Criterion for the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Analytically continue the grand-canonical partition function to obtain the return amplitude; take fixed-μ β derivatives of log Z to obtain cumulants, then use moment–cumulant relations and Lanczos recursion to construct early-time spread complexity.

Establishing a physical rate correspondence is an outcome to investigate, not a premise needed to organize the question.
